$comment: HISTORICAL APPLIED-MIGRATION IMMUTABILITY ATTESTATION (GOV-H, 2026-11-01).
WHAT THIS IS, AND WHAT IT IS NOT. The production migration ledger is DATA, in
a database scripts/check-migration-quality.js must never connect to (that gate
is deterministic, read-only, no DB, no network, no secrets, and runs in a
required status check). The boundary therefore cannot be READ here. It can only
be ATTESTED, with provenance.
The claim the gate makes from this file is deliberately weaker than "nothing
applied has changed", and is therefore true:
nothing at or below the LAST ATTESTED boundary has changed since that
attestation.
It never asserts the attestation is current. Three things keep it from quietly
becoming a lie:
1. any content change, deletion or rename at or below the boundary FAILS;
2. a NEW file numbered at or below the boundary FAILS (a migration written
into already-applied history);
3. the gate prints versions_above_boundary on every run, so an attestation
that has stopped tracking reality is visible in its own output rather than
silently narrowing coverage.
HOW TO RE-ATTEST (operator, parent-gated). A production ledger read is required
and is NOT something this gate may do for itself. Steps: read
supabase_migrations.schema_migrations max(version) under the read-only role;
set ledger_max to it; re-pin digests for every top-level migration at or below
it; record attested_at, attested_from and evidence_class. Raising ledger_max
without a ledger read is forging the attestation.
A LEDGER ENTRY PROVES A VERSION WAS RECORDED. It does NOT prove WHICH SOURCE
FILE was applied: 56 version prefixes on origin/main are shared by 170 files,
so for those versions the ledger cannot identify the file. This attestation
pins the file CONTENT regardless, which is the property that matters here --
whatever ran, the repository text has not moved since.
evidence_class: PRODUCTION_CATALOG_VERIFIED for ledger_max (2026-11-01 production inventory: 93 rows, 93 distinct versions, no duplicates, max 20270111000003); CODE_VERIFIED for every digest (hashed from the origin/main worktree at 5025f51d).
